subject: Renewal-topup: mid-contract capacity scaling & discount guardrails
messages:
From: Kelly Robinson <kelly@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@greenlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: mid-contract top-up + path to co-term at renewal

Hi Mina,

Hope you’re well — Greenline is seeing a stronger-than-expected lift in inference usage and we expect to need a ~40% capacity top-up for the remainder of this year. We’re interested in two things:

1) A mid-contract top-up quote (monthly committed units) and what the uplift pricing would look like versus our current rate.
2) The easiest path to co-term the added capacity with our Jan 2027 renewal, and whether any pro‑rata or voucher approach would reduce immediate invoice impact.

Attached a Q3 usage export and the current SOW for reference. We’ll need procurement and finance sign-off, so please include any standard timelines for amendment + PO.

Can you get me a few options by Friday? Happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Kelly
Kelly Robinson
Head of Cloud Ops, Greenline Health
kelly@greenlinehealth.com
+1 415-555-0142

Attachments: greenline-usage-q3.csv (csv), Greenline_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kelly Robinson <kelly@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract top-up + path to co-term at renewal

Thanks Kelly — appreciate the heads up and the data. I pulled the usage and sketched three practical options that balance near-term cash impact vs. unit economics:

Option A — Immediate committed top-up (preferred for predictability)- +40% committed units for Oct–Dec at current committed pricing; 6% uplift discount on the incremental units if you accept an early annualization clause that rolls the top-up into the Jan 2027 renewal. Immediate invoice reflects full additional commit.

Option B — Top-up with voucher smoothing- Add the +40% commit now, but we issue a one-time voucher (applied across Q4 invoices) equal to 50% of the uplift delta to soften the hit. Co-terminates with Jan 2027 automatically.

Option C — Usage buffer (minimal change to invoicing)- Keep current commit, add a short-term burst buffer (pay-as-you-go up to the +40% level). No invoice change up front; higher per-token rate for buffer consumption. Co-term must be negotiated at renewal.

Internal notes: I’ve looped in Marissa for discount approvals and Ben for billing cadence / PO flow.

If one of these looks promising I’ll run the exact numbers and fill in pro‑rata amounts and an amendment draft for legal. Would you like a quick call tomorrow to walk through?

Best,
Mina
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Mina / Ben — quick take: Option B is structurally attractive for Greenline (helps procurement) while protecting our unit economics. Approve up to a 6% effective concession on the incremental units if we require co‑term and an annualization clause at renewal.

Ben, can finance accept voucher accounting for Q4 (applied across the invoices) and still meet our revenue recognition? If not, we default back to Option A with a smaller immediate concession (3–4%).

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Marissa / Mina — finance confirms voucher smoothing is workable if we treat the voucher as a contra-revenue credit applied at invoice and with an explicit expiration tied to the amendment (we’d recognize the revenue net of voucher when invoiced). That keeps our ARR cleaner and meets accounting controls.

Specifically: up to a 6% voucher on the delta units applied evenly across Oct/Nov/Dec invoices; co‑term requirement and annualization clause must be signed by both parties in the amendment. We’ll need procurement PO by Oct 5 to meet Q4 billing cadence.

I’ll draft the billing note and the voucher schedule — Mina, if you’re comfortable with Option B I’ll prepare the finance language for the amendment.

Ben
Director, Finance Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kelly Robinson <kelly@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract top-up + path to co-term at renewal

Kelly — thanks for waiting. Based on your ask and internal approvals here’s the recommended path (Option B):

- Add +40% committed units effective Oct 1.
- Redwood issues a one-time voucher equal to 50% of the uplift delta on incremental units (effectively a step-down on the first three invoices).
- Voucher applied evenly across Oct / Nov / Dec invoices (we’ll include voucher lines on each invoice).
- Co-term: the top-up will automatically annualize into your Jan 2027 renewal; amendment will include an annualization clause (rolls the incremental commit into the renewal baseline).
- Finance requires procurement PO by Oct 5 for Q4 billing; Legal will prepare a short amendment and DocuSign link.

Next steps: I’ll send the formal amendment + voucher schedule and a HubSpot record for approvals. If you want tighter up-front reduction instead of a voucher, we can do Option A with a 4% concession on incremental units — let me know.

Would you like me to set up the DocuSign now?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
